dedupe_keys.name: rail topology ontology rto owl base ontology for railway infrastructure topology

description: The Rail Topology Ontology is an OWL ontology that models the topology of railway infrastructure, so that engineering tools for planned and built rail networks can share one semantic model instead of exchanging XML and UML-based formats. It aligns with the UIC RailTopoModel and the railML and ISO 15926 part 14 work, and is organised into packages for base concepts, networks, network entities, topology and positioning, with SPARQL queries that derive directed reachability between track elements. Stefan Bischof and Gottfried Schenner of Siemens AG Österreich published it with a 2021 paper. Coverage is generic railway infrastructure. Format and access: an RDF/OWL file at a permanent W3ID address, which resolves to Siemens' GitHub Pages, and an entry in Linked Open Vocabularies. Licence: MPL-2.0 (weak copyleft), as stated in the paper; free. Caveats: it covers topology and positioning, not signalling or asset condition, and version 1.0 appears not to have been updated since. It supports network models and digital twins of rail infrastructure built as knowledge graphs. Related catalogue records are the ERA ontology for European railway infrastructure and the Brick building ontology, an equivalent for buildings.
